defect_observations.observation: The plateau computation says the stage prefixes less than b 'contribute' their probability but never states that their stage intervals lie wholly left of the plateau, and it never says that the intervals of larger prefixes lie wholly to the right and so contribute zero. The order follows from the successor display at lines 533-537 (bit 0 lower, bit 1 upper) plus nesting, but the step is left implicit. The rest of the computation is written, so this is not counted as a coverage gap.

The identification with the source's distribution argues uniqueness among continuous functions. The source (printed p. 13) instead defines F by its plateau values and extension 'using monotonicity'. The handbook cdf is monotone and takes every value the source specifies, so it qualifies as that extension, but the text never states this bridge.

The source (printed p. 468) also says 'mu_1 is singular with respect to mu_2' for this relation. The definition does not record that alias, yet body line 317 uses 'singular with respect to Lebesgue measure'. The meaning can be recovered from the symmetric definition.

The source (printed p. 468) calls a set all of whose subsets have measure 0 a 'null set'. The handbook renames it 'signed-null', which avoids a clash with mu-null sets, but it nowhere maps the new term to the source's term.

The proof asserts that (D^c,D) is a Hahn partition, and gives the two restriction formulas, without the one-line check: alpha equals nu_1 on subsets of D^c because nu_2(D^c)=0, and equals -nu_2 on subsets of D because nu_1(D)=0. This is the same level of detail as the source (p. 468).

The statement promises 'the distinction between a zero total value and a signed-null set'. Within C003's own proof this is only a closing remark. The worked instance is at annex lines 628-639 (C018 item 2) and the signed-null criterion is in the w02b-p15-005 annex at lines 80-86. Both are on route, so the promise is met across the section, but it depends on those other entries.

The phrase 'The subset argument for negative sets is identical' is a 'similarly'-type phrase. The omitted argument is the single inclusion step written at line 48 and has no sign-dependent step, so it is not counted as a gap. The negative-union case is written out in full.
